newsitem.title: UK: Thames Water shares firm after annual results.
newsitem.headline: Thames Water shares firm after annual results.

text.p: Shares in Thames Water Plc were marked up in pre-market trade on Tuesday after the company reported full-year profits at the top end of expectations.
The company posted annual pre-tax, pre-exceptional profits of 384 million stg, outstripping most forecasts which ranged from 350-384 million. The total dividend, at 34.4p, was in line with forecasts.
The shares were up eight pence at 688 by 0720 GMT.

Thames said its new businesses should provide a strong earnings stream and it should maintain real dividend growth. It said it had cut the amount of water leaking out of pipes by a quarter since a peak in 1995 and aimed to halve leakage by 2000.

"They've come out with a pretty good set of figures and the market seems to like the look of them," one market-maker said. "But now it's a question of waiting to see what kind of tax they get hit with, so they won't go too high."
The new British government plans to impose a windfall tax on privatised utilities. It will be announced in a special budget on July 2.
Other water shares were also marked up ahead of the official market opening, with Severn Trent Plc up four at 744 and United Utilities Plc 1-1/2p higher at 655.
